newsitem.title: USA: Court invalidates Los Angeles Cty relief measure.
newsitem.headline: Court invalidates Los Angeles Cty relief measure.

text.p: A judge has ruled that legislation that helped Los Angeles County balance its budget violated the state Constitution, the county said on Tuesday.
The 1995 fiscal relief legislation authorized the transfer of $50 million of Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority sales tax funds to the county.
But a Superior Court judge has found that the legislation violated a provision of the state Constitution that prohibits "special legislation," the county said.

County officials said the decision was unfortunate for the county, which sought the transit funds during its budget crisis. Officials said, however, that the trial court's action would be stayed pending an appeal.

"We're a long way from having to write a check," said Joel Bellman, a spokesman for Zev Yaroslavsky, chairman of the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors. "The bottom line is it's too early to tell what the fiscal impact will be. We'll have a better idea when our appeals are exhausted."
